recipes.title: Silky Cardamom Rasmalai
recipes.excerpt: Soft chenna rounds steeped in saffron milk, finished with freshly crushed cardamom and pistachio.
recipes.imageAlt: A creamy Indian-inspired dessert topped with soft cream
ingredients: 2 tablespoons lemon juice, mixed with 2 tablespoons water
steps: Bring 750 ml of the milk to a gentle boil. Turn off the heat, add the diluted lemon juice a little at a time, and stir until the curds separate.
Strain the curds through a clean muslin cloth. Rinse briefly with cool water, then hang for 25 minutes so the chenna is moist but not dripping.
Knead the chenna until smooth and supple. Divide into 8 portions and shape into small, even discs.
Boil the sugar with 4 cups of water. Add the discs, cover, and cook at a lively simmer for 12 minutes. Let them cool in the syrup.
Warm the remaining milk with saffron and crushed cardamom. Simmer until lightly reduced, then cool.
Gently squeeze excess syrup from each disc and place them in the saffron milk. Chill for at least 2 hours and finish with pistachios.
recipes.tip: Crush the cardamom just before warming the milk; the fragrance stays brighter.

recipes.title: Everyday Elaichi Chai
recipes.excerpt: A familiar cup made more memorable with freshly cracked green cardamom and a patient simmer.
recipes.imageAlt: A freshly brewed cup of chai with spices
ingredients: 1 to 2 teaspoons sugar, or to taste
steps: Bring the water and crushed cardamom to a gentle boil for 2 minutes.
Add the tea leaves and simmer for 1 minute, until the water turns a deep amber.
Pour in the milk and add sugar. Bring back to a gentle simmer, watching carefully so the tea does not boil over.
Strain into warm cups and serve straight away.
recipes.tip: For a stronger cup, steep the tea leaves a little longer before adding milk.
recipes.imageTitle: A freshly brewed cup of elaichi milk tea with aromatic spices.

recipes.title: Sunday Cardamom Chicken Biryani
recipes.excerpt: Layered basmati, tender chicken and whole spices come together in a fragrant, family-style dum.
recipes.imageAlt: A bowl of chicken biryani with basmati rice and herbs
ingredients: 300 g basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
5 green cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick and 4 cloves
A pinch of saffron soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
steps: Mix the chicken with yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste and salt. Leave to marinate while you prepare the rice.
Fry the onions in ghee until golden. Set aside half for layering. Add the whole spices to the pan, then add the marinated chicken and cook for 12 minutes.
Boil the rice in salted water until it is about 70 percent cooked. Drain well.
Spread half the rice over the chicken. Add herbs and some fried onions, then layer the remaining rice on top.
Drizzle the saffron milk over the rice. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently from the sides and bring the layers to the table.
recipes.tip: Keep the cardamom pods whole so they perfume the rice without overpowering it.
recipes.imageTitle: Chicken biryani with basmati rice and herbs.

recipes.title: Coconut & Cardamom Ladoo
recipes.excerpt: A quick festive sweet with toasted coconut, gentle sweetness and a bright finish of elaichi.
recipes.imageAlt: Traditional Indian sweets arranged for a festive table
ingredients: 2 cups unsweetened desiccated coconut, plus extra for rolling
steps: Warm a wide pan over low heat. Toast the coconut for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the condensed milk and cardamom. Stir continuously until the mixture thickens and begins to pull away from the pan.
Fold in the cashews if using. Let the mixture cool until comfortable to handle.
Grease your palms lightly and roll into small balls. Coat with extra coconut and leave to set for 15 minutes.
recipes.tip: Keep the heat low; coconut can turn from fragrant to toasted very quickly.
recipes.imageTitle: Traditional coconut and cardamom sweets arranged for a festive table.

recipes.title: Cardamom Pistachio Iced Coffee
recipes.excerpt: A cool, creamy coffee with a whisper of cardamom and a nutty pistachio finish.
recipes.imageAlt: Green cardamom pods and whole spices on a dark surface
ingredients: 1 double shot of espresso or ½ cup strong chilled coffee
1 tablespoon pistachio syrup or pistachio cream
A pinch of freshly ground cardamom
Ice and crushed pistachios to finish
steps: Stir the espresso with pistachio syrup and a small pinch of cardamom.
Fill a tall glass with ice and pour in the cold milk.
Slowly pour the coffee mixture over the milk. Finish with crushed pistachios and serve.
recipes.tip: Start with only a pinch of cardamom; its citrusy aroma is lovely when kept subtle.
recipes.imageTitle: Green cardamom pods and whole spices beside a cold coffee.

recipes.title: Slow-Simmered Elaichi Payasam
recipes.excerpt: A gently reduced milk pudding with tender rice, golden nuts and the delicate warmth of cardamom.
recipes.imageAlt: A creamy dessert served with a festive finish
ingredients: ¼ cup basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
⅓ cup sugar, or to taste
steps: Warm the ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and toast the cashews and raisins until golden. Set aside.
Drain the rice. Bring the milk to a gentle simmer in the same pan, then add the rice.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is soft and the milk has thickened.
Stir in the sugar, crushed cardamom and saffron. Simmer for another 3 minutes.
Fold in the toasted nuts. Serve warm, or chill and serve cold.
recipes.tip: Stir along the base of the pan often so the milk reduces evenly.
recipes.imageTitle: Creamy elaichi payasam served with a festive finish.

recipes.title: Cardamom Pistachio Latte
recipes.excerpt: Espresso, velvety milk and pistachio meet a subtle, fragrant note of freshly ground elaichi.
recipes.imageAlt: Fresh green cardamom pods and whole spices
ingredients: 1 double shot espresso or ½ cup strong coffee
¾ cup milk of your choice
1 tablespoon pistachio cream or pistachio syrup
A small pinch of freshly ground cardamom
steps: Warm the milk gently with pistachio cream, stirring until smooth. Do not let it boil.
Brew the espresso into a mug and stir in the cardamom.
Pour the pistachio milk over the espresso and finish with crushed pistachios.
recipes.tip: If your pistachio cream is sweetened, taste before adding anything extra.
recipes.imageTitle: Fresh green cardamom pods and whole spices for a pistachio latte.

blogsPage.title: Stories with a little more warmth.

blogs.title: Four small signs of fragrant cardamom
blogs.excerpt: A simple guide to looking, smelling and storing cardamom so its character stays part of the meal.
blogs.imageAlt: Green cardamom pods with aromatic whole spices

sections.heading: Start with the pod
paragraphs: Choose pods that feel intact and substantial for their size. Natural variation in colour is normal; freshness is better judged by the pod's aroma and condition than by a single shade of green.
If the pods are badly crushed or very dry, some of their aroma may already have escaped.

sections.heading: Let the aroma tell you more
paragraphs: Crush one pod gently between your fingers. A good pod should open with a lively, sweet, citrus-like fragrance. A faint or flat smell can be a sign that it has been stored for a long time or left exposed to air.

sections.heading: Keep it whole until you need it
paragraphs: Whole pods protect their seeds from air and light. Store them in a tightly closed container in a cool, dry cupboard, then crack or grind only the amount you plan to use.

sections.heading: A little goes a long way
paragraphs: Cardamom can be gently fragrant or boldly aromatic depending on how much you use. Start small, taste, and add more if the dish needs it.

blogs.imageTitle: Fresh green cardamom pods and whole spices for a buying guide.

blogs.title: Whole or ground? How to use cardamom in the kitchen
blogs.excerpt: Choose the right form for chai, a slow-cooked curry, a delicate dessert or a quick weekday bake.
blogs.imageAlt: Ground cardamom shown in a step-by-step cooking preparation.

sections.heading: Whole pods for a slow infusion
paragraphs: Use whole, lightly cracked pods when you want cardamom to perfume a liquid over time. They work beautifully in chai, rice, custards and slow-simmered sauces, and can be removed before serving.

sections.heading: Ground seeds for an even finish
paragraphs: Freshly ground seeds blend smoothly into cake batter, cookie dough and spice mixes. Grind only what you need so the aroma does not fade while it waits in the jar.

sections.heading: Match the form to the dish
paragraphs: A whole pod gives a gentle, gradual note. Ground cardamom reaches every bite and tastes more immediate. When a recipe is flexible, begin with a small amount and adjust to taste.

blogs.imageTitle: Ground cardamom being prepared for use in the kitchen.

blogs.title: The everyday rituals that begin with elaichi
blogs.excerpt: A crushed pod in morning tea, a pinch in payasam: cardamom makes ordinary pauses feel considered.
blogs.imageAlt: A warm cup of Indian chai with spices

sections.heading: A familiar cup, made your own
paragraphs: In many homes, cardamom is part of the tea tin and the morning routine. A pod or two can make the kitchen smell welcoming before the first cup reaches the table.

sections.heading: The finishing touch in sweets
paragraphs: A small pinch of ground elaichi can lift rice pudding, milk sweets and festive bakes. Add it near the end of cooking so its delicate fragrance stays present.

sections.heading: Share the moment
paragraphs: The best rituals are rarely complicated. Brew an extra cup, set out a small plate of something sweet and let the conversation take its time.

blogs.imageTitle: A warm cup of Indian chai served with spices.

blogs.title: Cardamom belongs in savoury cooking, too
blogs.excerpt: From fragrant rice to a slow-cooked stew, whole pods add a floral, warm note beyond dessert.
blogs.imageAlt: Biryani rice layered with herbs and spices

sections.heading: Let the whole spice bloom
paragraphs: Add lightly bruised pods to warm oil or ghee with other whole spices. A short, gentle sizzle helps release their fragrance before the rice, vegetables or broth go in.

sections.heading: Keep the balance
paragraphs: Cardamom is distinctive, so pair it with intention. Cinnamon, cloves, cumin and black pepper make familiar companions, but the right balance depends on the dish.

sections.heading: Finish with freshness
paragraphs: For a brighter note, crush a seed or two and stir them in just before serving. The aroma will meet the steam as the dish reaches the table.

csrPage.title: Goodness grows when we grow together.
csrPage.description: We believe a responsible business should care for the people and places behind every ingredient. Our focus is to listen, build useful partnerships and share progress with honesty.
csrPage.heroImageAlt: Green Kerala hills and tree-covered growing landscapes
csrPage.introText: Our roots are in a place, a craft and the people who make it possible. We want our work to create value beyond the product: through respectful relationships, thoughtful use of resources and community partnerships shaped by real needs.

commitments.title: People and livelihoods
commitments.text: We aim to build long-term relationships with the people and partners connected to our supply chain, with respect for skill, experience and fair opportunity.

commitments.title: Health and wellbeing
commitments.text: We see access to care as an important part of a thriving community. We will work with trusted local partners where our contribution can be useful and accountable.

commitments.title: Care for the land
commitments.text: Healthy growing landscapes support both livelihoods and the ingredients we value. We are committed to learning how our choices can support more responsible sourcing.

csrPage.communityTitle: Listen first. Work together. Share progress.
csrPage.communityText: Good community work begins with listening. We want to learn from local organisations and communities, support initiatives with clear purpose, and be transparent about what has been done and what still needs work.
csrPage.communityImageAlt: A healthcare professional in a clinic, shown as an illustrative image
csrPage.communityImageNote: Illustrative photo; it does not depict an Elacher Ghor programme.
csrPage.closingText: We will use this space to share verified initiatives and measurable progress as partnerships develop. For community or sustainability enquiries, contact our team.
